computation.p_e_t_given_e_t_minus_1_formula: mean_e(P(e in top_k(t) | e in top_k(t-1)))
computation.chance_baseline_formula: top_k / n_experts (expected overlap fraction under independent/memoryless routing)

finding: Both route-transition metrics sit ~4.3-4.1x above the chance baseline for independent/memoryless routing (9.4%): on average 40.5% of the 6 routed experts persist from one token position to the next (vs 9.4% expected by chance), and a given expert that was routed has a 38.2% chance of being routed again next position (vs 9.4% chance). This is genuine, decisive route-transition predictability -- R-predictable-route-prefetch's condition ('route transition predictable, P(E_t|E_t-1) peaked') is CONFIRMED for O003, with a solid effective sample (2340 transition-events across 26 layers, not just the 91 raw tokens).
